I implemented the streaming layer in three new source files under `libs/sdk-py/langgraph_sdk/stream/` (plus package `__init__.py` files):

### `multi_cursor_buffer.py` — `MultiCursorBuffer[T]`
A generic append-only async buffer. `__aiter__` returns a fresh cursor that replays all buffered items from index 0, then suspends on a per-iterator future until `push()` wakes it or `close()` releases it cleanly. `_wakeups` is a `set` of suspended-iterator futures, so `len(_wakeups)` equals the number of currently-suspended iterators.

### `subscription.py` — channel/subscription logic
- `normalize_segment` — strips colon-suffix.
- `is_prefix_match` — normalizes namespace segments; prefix segments containing a colon are matched as exact literals; empty prefix matches anything; longer prefix fails.
- `namespace_matches` — `None`/empty prefixes ⇒ `True`; depth limit rejects deeper namespaces; otherwise any prefix match.
- `infer_channel` — method→channel map, plus `custom` → `custom:{name}` (or bare `custom`), `None` for unknown.
- `matches_subscription` — channel membership (bare `custom` matches any `custom:*`) plus the optional `namespaces` filter.

### `transport/http.py` — `EventStreamHandle` + `ProtocolSseTransport`
- `EventStreamHandle` exposes `ready`/`done`/`events` properties and an async `close()`.
- `ProtocolSseTransport.send_command` — POSTs to `/threads/{id}/commands`; 200→parsed dict, 202→`None`, 4xx→`HTTPStatusError`, empty-200→`RuntimeError("...did not return a valid response")`, post-close→`RuntimeError("...closed")`.
